title: introduce-slowpath-capture-and-hot-prompt-sampler
author: Asha Patel
commits: a1f4d2b Introduce slowpath detector and API hook
b3e9c88 Add hot-prompt sampler, rate limiter and tests
c2d9f71 Dashboards: slowpath-radar and prompt-cohort panel; docs
description: Motivation: We see recurring high tail latency events where requests take a 'slowpath' through the runtime (kernel stalls, queue backpressure, or unexpected KV cache miss sequences) that aren't visible in coarse per-route percentiles. This PR adds a lightweight slowpath capture pipeline and a targeted hot-prompt sampler to help diagnose and correlate these events to prompt shape, tenant behavior, and kernel-level signals. Design: 1) slowpath_detector: in the serving runtime we add a low-overhead detector that marks invocations as slowpath when GPU queue wait > 25ms or stage stall > configured threshold. 2) structured capture: when an invocation is marked and a probabilistic sampler fires we emit a compact JSON trace with prompt fingerprint, stage timings, kernel tags, model_variant, small token-cost sketch (count & sketch digest), and a redacted prompt signature. 3) hot-prompt sampler: a frequency-based detector that promotes a fingerprint to "hot" when it appears > X times in Y minutes; while hot it collects higher-fidelity captures (including appendix token-level timing for first N tokens) behind a configurable cap to bound cost. 4) dashboards and alerts: add a new "Inference Slowpath Radar" dashboard (heatmap of slowpath density by model/region, prompt-cohort table, recent hot fingerprints) and an alert rule "hotprompt_surveillance" that fires when a hot fingerprint causes > P99 latency regressions across tenants; the alert includes dynamic cooldown and an adaptive sampling cap so we do not overload telemetry. Implementation notes: the detector emits to the existing telemetry ingestion with a new metric family slowpath.marker and a compact trace envelope slowpath.capture.v1. The hot-prompt sampler maintains an in-memory LRU frequency table with spill to Redis for Durable mode in Dedicated/Private deployments. Backwards compatibility: all captures are privacy-first: prompt bodies are hashed and redacted by default; telemetry consumers opt-in to higher fidelity. Tests: unit and integration tests for detector thresholds, sampler rate limits, redis spill behavior, and the dashboard JSON schema validator. Docs: includes operator guidance for tuning thresholds and cost caps and a migration note for Dedicated customers. Checklist: - [x] runtime detector implemented and benchmarked for <0.5% median CPU overhead - [x] structured capture schema and ingestion mapping added - [x] hot-prompt frequency algorithm with configurable caps - [x] dashboards and alert rule added and validated in staging - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] operator docs and runbook entries - [x] performance bench for worst-case sampling cost Rollout plan: feature is gated behind an observability flag (sdk flag + server-side gate). We will enable slowpath.marker export in staging for 48 hours, run the dashboard with synthetic slowpath injections, then enable hot-prompt promotions at 10% of production traffic for two weeks before increasing. Costs are bounded via a tenant-level sampling budget and global adaptive cap. Related: ENG-2241 (slowpath investigations), ENG-2305 (observability budget controls).
review_comments: Jordan Kim: Nice design. Two requests: make the default GPU queue threshold configurable via runtime config and add a guard to prevent Redis stampedes when many fingerprints promote simultaneously.
Author (Asha): Added runtime config flag --slowpath-queue-ms and implemented a jittered backoff for redis writes, see commit b3e9c88.
Miguel Ramirez: Can we ensure captures for private deployments never touch our hosted Redis endpoint? Also please document the privacy redaction explicitly in the operator runbook.
Author (Asha): Private/Dedicated default flips to local spill only; documented in docs/observability/slowpath.md. Added privacy section and sample KMS note.
Priya Singh: Tests look good. One nit: add a tiny end-to-end perf check that ensures worst-case sampling keeps p99 kernel latency change < 1%.
Author (Asha): Added end-to-end perf bench in tests/bench_slowpath_end2end.py and added results to PR body.
release_notes: Add slowpath capture and hot-prompt sampler: new low-overhead tracer for slow invocation paths and frequency-based hot-prompt promotion with bounded capture fidelity. Adds Slowpath Radar dashboard and a hotprompt_surveillance alert with adaptive caps. Operators can tune thresholds and sampling budgets. Backwards-compatible and privacy-preserving by default.
